pages.title: Publishing
pages.markdown:
# Publishing

## Build a static site

Run this from the directory containing `docs/`.

```sh
npx grimoire3d build
```

The output is `dist/` by default. To choose a different output directory, use `--out-dir site` or set `outDir: site` in `grimoire.yml`. The CLI protects existing files in an unrelated output directory.

pages.title: Publishing
pages.markdown:
## Upload the output

Publish the contents of the output directory with a static host such as Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages. This documentation uses GitHub Pages. Upload the complete output so chapter URLs, styles, images, and video work together. Chapter URLs have their own HTML files, so direct links work on a host that serves directory indexes.

For a site under a subpath, such as a GitHub Pages project at `https://example.github.io/handbook/`, include that path in `siteUrl` before you build.

[Configure your site metadata](./metadata.md) before you publish.

pages.title: Site settings and SEO
pages.markdown:
# Site settings and SEO

Place `grimoire.yml` next to `docs/`.

```yaml
title: Engineering Handbook
description: Setup, operations, and release notes for the project.
siteUrl: https://docs.example.com/
author: Documentation Team
socialImage: assets/share.avif
locale: en
magicMode: true
```

pages.title: Site settings and SEO
pages.markdown:
## Titles and social cards

The build produces standalone HTML for every chapter, including the text, navigation, page title, description, and Open Graph metadata. Visitors and crawlers can read the articles without JavaScript.

Set `siteUrl` to get canonical URLs and a sitemap. Set `socialImage` to an absolute HTTP(S) URL or an image path relative to `docs/`. At the domain root the build also emits `robots.txt` pointing to the sitemap.

pages.title: Site settings and SEO
pages.markdown:
## Chapter metadata

Supply `title`, `description`, or `socialImage` in a chapter's YAML front matter. A chapter-level image path is relative to that chapter.

```markdown
---
title: Deployment guide
description: Publish the project to a static web host.
socialImage: ./assets/deploy.avif
---
# Deployment
```

Share the URL for a chapter or a specific heading, for example `/read/publishing/metadata/#chapter-metadata`. Existing links that start with `#/` also work.
